paragraphs: Formal shoes are judged on the toe and the sole, and everything in between is convention. The shape of the last is the only part a maker really owns, which is why two pairs that look identical in a photograph feel entirely different on a foot.
The model is light at 16,688 polygons and 9,218 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits footwear and fashion visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, character accessories, advertising, film costume and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A military funeral is choreography, and the casket is the fixed point everything else is measured from. The flag is folded to a specific number of turns, the carry is rehearsed, and the whole ceremony exists to make an unbearable moment orderly.
The model holds 29,862 polygons and 31,382 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits film and television production, documentary and historical visualisation, ceremonial scenes, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The white finish on modern laboratory instruments is not styling. It shows contamination immediately, which is the same reason clinical surfaces are pale, and it separates current equipment from the black and grey of an older bench.
The model is light at 45,113 polygons and 23,264 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in white. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits laboratory and medical visualisation, scientific equipment marketing, e-commerce imagery, research interiors, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The B61 family has been in service longer than most of the aircraft that carried it, and it has been modernised repeatedly rather than replaced. The shape is familiar from museum displays and news graphics, where it stands in for the whole subject.
The model holds 63,665 polygons and 67,409 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $34 it suits news and documentary graphics, defence and policy visualisation, museum and education material, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The portable air conditioner is a compromise everybody knows is bad. Half the unit is inside the room it is cooling, the hose leaks heat back in, and it sells enormously because the alternative involves a landlord's permission.
The model is very light at 12,623 polygons and 13,569 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $34 it suits appliance and interior visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, residential and office scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A tournament table is slate under cloth, and the slate is why it weighs what it does. Nothing else stays flat to the tolerance the game needs, which is the reason a serious table is installed rather than delivered.
The model is light at 26,432 polygons and 14,327 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in black, and carries StemCell certification.
At $34 it suits leisure and venue visualisation, games room interiors, equipment marketing, e-commerce imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2024.

The retention balloon is what makes this device work and what makes it a permanent fixture of hospital care. It is inflated after insertion so the catheter cannot fall out, and that single mechanism has been in use for the better part of a century.
The model is very light at 10,020 polygons and 5,050 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so it runs in interactive material. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits medical device marketing, nursing and clinical education, patient explanation, technical documentation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

An empty stage is the most loaded object in theatre. It is a box with one side missing and a floor that is expected to be walked on hard, and every production that will ever happen on it starts from the same rectangle.

The model holds 61,905 polygons and 61,916 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 7 maps all at 8192x8192, which is what the floor and drapes require at that scale. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits theatre and venue visualisation, event and production presentation, film and television sets, game environments, previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

An XRF gun tells you what an alloy is in a few seconds without cutting it. Scrap yards, refineries and museums all use the same device for completely different reasons, and all of them are answering the same question: what is this actually made of.
The model is light at 16,374 polygons and 17,513 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in yellow, and carries StemCell certification.
At $33 it suits industrial and laboratory visualisation, instrument marketing, e-commerce imagery, inspection and recycling scenes, training material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A can in ice rather than a bottle changes the register entirely. It is casual, immediate and unpretentious, which is exactly the positioning a great many drinks brands spend a fortune trying to achieve.
The model holds 35,478 polygons and 36,135 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, supplying the bucket together with the can. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $33 it suits beverage and packaging visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, bar and event scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Candy floss is sugar spun into threads by centrifugal force, and the machine is a heated spinning bowl and nothing else. The product is almost entirely air, which is why it costs what it does and why it cannot be packaged well.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the machine together with the candy as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $32 the set suits fairground and event visualisation, food and retail imagery, advertising, film sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

A millstone works by shearing rather than crushing, which is why the grooves cut into the face matter more than the weight. Dressing those grooves was a skilled trade, and a stone that had been dressed badly ruined the flour.
The model is supplied in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $31 it suits historical and heritage visualisation, museum and education work, rural and period scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A double pushchair is a packaging problem with a deadline. Two children, one set of hands, and a frame that still has to fit through a shop door, which is why side by side and inline layouts both exist and neither has won.
The model holds 103,670 polygons and 53,829 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a second build is offered separately.
At $31 it suits product and retail visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, advertising, street and interior scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A changing room is the highest converting square metre in any shop, and it is furnished accordingly: a mirror angled to flatter, a hook within reach of somebody half dressed, and a seat for the bag rather than the customer.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the equipment as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $31 the set suits retail and interior visualisation, shopfitting and equipment marketing, store scenes, advertising, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2024.
